quotes.text: Power Platform is not a democratization tool. In reality, it is a control plane designed for capturing enterprise value that your organization is systematically hemorrhaging through manual entropy.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes Power Platform from a citizen-developer toy into an economic control plane.

quotes.text: The governance model is the only thing that keeps this from becoming shadow IT chaos but structured governance is not about being restrictive. It is about being an enabler.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Positions governance as the enabler of citizen development rather than a brake.

quotes.text: You have to understand that compliance is not a technology problem. It is a documentation and evidence problem.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why structured workflows that capture evidence solve audit pain.

quotes.text: The real power is that co-pilot is not replacing your developers, it is amplifying your business users.

quotes.text: The power platform is not a replacement for pro code. It is a necessary complement that allows professional developers to focus on complex logic and high level architecture.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

Arbitrage plays: forms, AP/AR, compliance, frontline apps and approvals
Dataverse, RPA and AI Builder with Copilot
Workflow debt, M&A integration kits and licensing arbitrage
Governance, measuring ROI and the competitive moat
Objections, the transformation path and the closing argument

takeaways: Power Platform delivers capabilities at a fraction of pro-code cost and in weeks instead of months, which turns manual processes into a measurable arbitrage opportunity.
Scaling depends on a citizen developer model backed by zoned governance, DLP policies, RBAC and a Center of Excellence, so speed does not turn into shadow IT.
Choosing the right licensing model, such as per flow licensing for shared high-volume processes, and measuring ROI rigorously decide whether the program keeps its funding.
hook: Many organizations see Power Platform as a tool for hobby apps while manual work, slow approvals and expensive pro-code projects drain their budgets. This episode shows IT leaders, architects and finance stakeholders where the low-code arbitrage lies, from AP automation and compliance evidence to RPA, Dataverse and licensing, and how governance makes it scale safely.
